# FetchCore Repository Knowledge, Retrieval, and Serving Boundaries

## Canonical source of truth

Repository sources pass through materialization, safe scanning, corpus/document policy, and `RepositoryIndexer` extraction. The canonical unit is `KnowledgeDocument`, carrying typed `KnowledgeEvidence`, `KnowledgeProvenance`, repository, revision, path, line span, and checksum. KnowledgePacks and source-derived relationships enrich this knowledge but do not make a source authoritative. Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, and other indexes are rebuildable projections, not canonical storage; changing or rebuilding a vendor schema must not redefine source evidence. Sources: `docs/architecture/repository-knowledge.md`, `docs/architecture/projection.md`.

## Intent, scope, and execution policy

`SearchIntent` declares retrieval meaning independently of corpus authorization and execution policy. Its v2 fields include the unchanged `canonical_query`, required `anchors`, an optional required `SearchExpression` tree (`Term`, `Anchor`, `AllOf`, `AnyOf`), caller-attributed `expansions`, weak `hints`, typed `signals`, and v1-compatible exact/semantic terms. FetchCore does not infer anchors, boolean structure, or synonyms from natural language. Expansions increase recall without relaxing required structure; hints remain preferences.

`SearchScope` defines where and how broadly retrieval may operate: workspace, repository, revision, repository paths, knowledge types, maximum results, mode, settings, and optional retrieval configuration. `SearchRequirement` is a bounded allocation hint, not a satisfaction decision. `RetrievalConfig` selects acquisition behavior such as lexical, dense, or hybrid mode. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`, `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`.

## Unsupported required semantics

The policy is fail-closed rejection. There is no configurable flattening fallback. Before scanning, backend I/O, or embedding, adapters validate whether every participating channel can preserve required canonical text, anchors, and expressions. Unsupported required constructs raise `KnowledgeSearchError` with category `unsupported_semantics` and translation policy `reject`. Optional expansions, hints, and signals may remain unconsumed and be reported as `partially_unsupported` without rejecting retrieval. Hybrid currently rejects anchors or boolean groups because fusion cannot guarantee those constraints and there is no post-fusion constraint engine. Unsupported retrieval modes likewise raise a typed `unsupported_capability` error; FetchCore does not silently substitute lexical for dense or vice versa. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## Current retrieval channels and adapters

Current acquisition paths are local lexical scanning, backend lexical/BM25, dense vector retrieval, and backend hybrid retrieval where advertised capabilities permit them. Built-in retrieval adapters are `local-semantic` (local lexical scanning), `solr` (lexical/dense/hybrid plus current operational index synchronization), `opensearch` (lexical/dense/hybrid), and `qdrant-vector` (dense and hybrid vector/sparse acquisition; standalone lexical is not implied). `ollama` is a separate embedding provider, not a retrieval backend. The backend-neutral `KnowledgeSearchBackend.search(intent, scope, requirements)` port returns `KnowledgeSearchResponse` containing provenance-preserving `SearchResult` evidence. Graph traversal, a general identifier-first targeted router, and federated multi-repository fusion are not current mandatory retrieval paths. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`.

## Hybrid baseline

Hybrid independently acquires lexical or sparse candidates and dense candidates, then fuses them with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), the configured baseline. `RetrievalConfig` currently accepts only `rrf` as its hybrid strategy. Optional reranking occurs after acquisition and is bounded by an explicit candidate window; reranking is not a backend capability gate. Scores and fusion ranks are retrieval observations, not correctness, satisfaction, or authority. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## MCP serving boundary

The serving path is `MCP stdio → application runtime bootstrap → RetrievalApplicationService → KnowledgeSearchBackend`. MCP is a transport adapter: it exposes `search` and bounded `get_source`, but does not call Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, or local backend APIs directly and does not own retrieval translation or agent lifecycle. The application service creates repository-scoped requests, bounds result/source reads, and rejects unauthorized paths through a `RepositoryBinding`. P0 binds one authorized repository per server process; federated MCP search, HTTP/auth/ACL serving, `find_symbol`, and graph-backed `get_related` are deferred. Sources: `docs/architecture/serving.md`, `docs/guides/mcp.md`.

# FetchCore Repository Knowledge, Retrieval, and Serving Architecture

Evidence below reflects repository revision `e0145894d5b1c0f74c3ba8c9b228556ea7d6d81c`.

## Canonical source of truth

Repository sources pass through materialization, safe scanning, corpus/document policy, and `RepositoryIndexer` extraction. The canonical unit is `KnowledgeDocument` in `repository/indexing.py`, carrying typed `KnowledgeEvidence`, `KnowledgeProvenance`, repository/revision/path, line span, and checksum. KnowledgePacks and source-derived relationships enrich canonical knowledge but do not make a source automatically authoritative.

Canonical Repository Knowledge is backend-neutral. `projection/core.py` compiles it into `ProjectedKnowledgeRecord`; search and vector stores are rebuildable projections. Solr, OpenSearch, and Qdrant schemas do not define source-document meaning. A graph projection is only a future possibility, not a required current architecture hop. Sources: `docs/architecture/repository-knowledge.md`, `docs/architecture/projection.md`, `docs/architecture/overview.md`.

FetchCore's governing boundary is retrieval ≠ satisfaction ≠ authority. Results and scores are acquisition observations; consumers decide whether evidence is sufficient or correct and whether actions are authorized.

## SearchIntent, SearchScope, and execution configuration

`SearchIntent` represents query meaning. Its v2 fields are canonical query text; required top-level anchors; an optional required `Term | Anchor | AllOf | AnyOf` expression; caller-declared expansions with origins; weak hints; typed signals; and v1-compatible exact/semantic terms. Supported anchor kinds are `identifier`, `qualified_symbol`, `path`, `route`, and `source_ref`. Top-level anchors are ANDed. `AllOf` requires every child and `AnyOf` at least one child within a single retrieved record. Expansions add recall without relaxing required anchors or branches.

`SearchScope` carries the authorized workspace/repository, revision, paths, knowledge types, result bound, mode, runtime settings, and optional `RetrievalConfig`. `RetrievalConfig` selects lexical, dense, hybrid, reranking, and LTR execution behavior. Scope and execution configuration do not belong in intent. All are acquisition inputs, not consumer satisfaction rules.

The application passes `SearchRequest.query` unchanged as `canonical_query`; it does not infer anchors, Boolean branches, or synonyms from natural language. `QuerySignal.required` retains legacy weighting meaning and is not a hard filter; hard requirements must use an anchor or expression. Source: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`.

## Unsupported required semantics

The policy is reject, with no configurable flattening fallback. Participating channels validate intent before backend I/O, scanning, or embedding. Canonical text requires canonical-query support; anchors and expressions require effective channel support. Unsupported required constructs raise `KnowledgeSearchError(category="unsupported_semantics")` with channel, unsupported constructs, reason, and `translation_policy: reject`.

Optional expansions, hints, and signals may remain unconsumed without rejecting acquisition. Translation observations distinguish `preserved`, `partially_unsupported`, `rejected`, and `broadened`; no current successful path emits `broadened`. Rejected structure is never concatenated into embedding text.

Solr/OpenSearch lexical channels support canonical queries, required anchor filters, and nested Boolean filters. Local lexical and dense channels do not support required anchors or expressions. Qdrant supports canonical text but not required anchors/groups. Solr/OpenSearch hybrid also rejects anchors/groups because dense candidates plus current post-fusion processing cannot guarantee those constraints; there is no post-fusion constraint engine. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`.

## Current retrieval channels and backends

The backend-neutral `KnowledgeSearchBackend` port receives `SearchIntent`, `SearchScope`, and `SearchRequirement` values and returns `KnowledgeSearchResponse` containing `SearchResult` evidence.

Current acquisition channels are local lexical scanning, backend lexical/BM25 retrieval, dense vector retrieval, and backend hybrid retrieval where advertised capabilities permit. Built-in retrieval IDs are:

- `local-semantic`: local repository scanning and lexical acquisition.
- `solr`: Solr retrieval and operational index synchronization.
- `opensearch`: OpenSearch retrieval.
- `qdrant-vector`: Qdrant dense and hybrid vector/sparse acquisition.

`ollama` is an `EmbeddingProvider`, separate from retrieval backends. Adapters live under `adapters/retrieval/{local,solr,opensearch,qdrant}`; composition in `application/composition.py` owns concrete backend/provider registries. Unsupported requested modes fail explicitly rather than silently substituting lexical or dense behavior. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `docs/architecture/adapters-and-composition.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`.

A generic identifier-first targeted router, adaptive budgets, graph expansion, structural graph lookup, and federated multi-repository fusion are not current capabilities.

## Hybrid fusion baseline

The preferred baseline is independent lexical and dense acquisition followed by reciprocal-rank fusion (RRF), then optional bounded post-acquisition reranking. RRF is the baseline unless a controlled benchmark supports an alternative. The backend-neutral fusion kernel defaults to strategy `rrf`; each channel contributes `1 / (k + rank)`, contributions are summed, and candidates preserve per-channel ranks, raw/normalized scores, and contributions. Reranking may reorder only an already acquired bounded candidate set. Sources: `AGENTS.md` lines 292-309; `src/fetchcore/retrieval/fusion.py` lines 148-330; `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`.

## MCP serving boundary

The serving path is MCP stdio → MCP adapter → application runtime bootstrap → `RetrievalApplicationService` → authorized `RepositoryBinding` → `KnowledgeSearchBackend`. MCP is a transport: it does not call Solr/OpenSearch/Qdrant directly, own retrieval semantics, or own an agent lifecycle.

P0 exposes two tools:

- `search(query, repository?, limit=1..100, knowledge_types?)`, returning the native bounded `KnowledgeSearchResponse` mapping with provenance and backend metadata.
- `get_source(source_ref, repository?, line_start?, line_end?, context_lines?)`, performing a bounded read within the authorized repository binding. Path traversal and resolved-path escape are rejected.

The current MCP process binds one authorized repository. Streamable HTTP, authentication, organization ACL providers, `find_symbol`, graph-backed `get_related`, and federated multi-repository search are deferred. Sources: `docs/architecture/serving.md`, `docs/guides/mcp.md`, `docs/reference/cli-mcp.md`.

# FetchCore Repository-Knowledge Architecture

At repository revision `e0145894d5b1c0f74c3ba8c9b228556ea7d6d81c`, the intended flow is repository sources → registry/collections → `RepositoryIndexer` → Canonical Repository Knowledge → `KnowledgePack`s and typed relationships → projections → retrieval API → CLI/MCP/SDK/API.

Canonical Repository Knowledge is the source of truth. Search indexes, vector stores, and graph stores are rebuildable projections, not canonical storage. Backend replacement must not change FetchCore contract meaning. Canonical `KnowledgeDocument` and `KnowledgeProvenance` include repository identity, revision, and source path; a path alone does not identify evidence across repositories or revisions.

Sources: `AGENTS.md:77-113`; `docs/adr/ADR-0001-backend-neutral-knowledge.md:19-22`; `docs/concepts/repository-identity.md:1-5`.

# Search Contracts and Required Semantics

`SearchIntent` states what the caller means to retrieve. `SearchScope` states where FetchCore may look. `RetrievalConfig`/policy states how retrieval executes. These concerns must remain separate: intent is not a generic configuration bag, and canonical meaning is distinct from scope, budgets, and backend policy. Expansions may improve recall without changing canonical query identity; hints must not silently become requirements.

Search scope carries a repository and authorized workspace. The serving application resolves a `RepositoryBinding` and restricts source access to it.

Unsupported required-semantics policy is `reject`; there is no configurable flattening fallback. Validation happens before backend I/O, scanning, or embedding. Canonical text requires canonical-query support. Anchors and expressions require effective lexical-channel support. A failure raises `KnowledgeSearchError` with category `unsupported_semantics`, translation policy `reject`, channel, reasons, and unsupported constructs.

Optional expansions, hints, and signals may remain unconsumed without rejecting acquisition. Translation observations distinguish `preserved`, `partially_unsupported`, `rejected`, and `broadened`; no current successful path emits `broadened`. Rejected structure is never concatenated into embedding text.

Hybrid retrieval still rejects hard anchors/groups because the current dense-plus-fusion pipeline has no post-fusion constraint engine and cannot guarantee them.

Sources: `AGENTS.md:225-259`; `docs/concepts/search-intent.md` (Translation and diagnostics); `src/fetchcore/retrieval/translation.py:62-99`; `docs/concepts/repository-identity.md:1-5`.

# Retrieval Channels, Backends, Fusion, and Serving

Current acquisition modes are lexical, dense, and hybrid when the selected backend advertises them. Built-in adapters are:

- `local-semantic`: local repository scanning and lexical acquisition.
- `solr`: Solr retrieval and current operational index synchronization.
- `opensearch`: OpenSearch retrieval.
- `qdrant-vector`: Qdrant dense and hybrid vector/sparse acquisition.
- `ollama`: embedding provider, separate from retrieval backends.

Mode capability checks are explicit. Lexical requires lexical support; dense requires dense support; hybrid requires dense and hybrid support. Unsupported requested modes raise typed errors—there is no implicit dense/lexical substitution. Solr and OpenSearch support canonical text, structured anchors, and boolean expressions on their lexical channels. Local and Qdrant advertise canonical text only. Dense participation never inherits lexical constraint support. Graph projection and federated search remain future work; operational CLI indexing currently targets Solr.

The preferred hybrid baseline is independent/parallel lexical and dense acquisition → reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) → optional bounded reranking. RRF remains the baseline unless a controlled benchmark demonstrates a better strategy.

Serving is backend-neutral and passes through the application service to CLI, MCP, and SDK/API consumers. Current MCP serving binds exactly one authorized repository per process; federated multi-repository ranking is future work. `RepositoryBinding` is the authorization/source-access boundary, while canonical provenance preserves repository, revision, and path identity.

Sources: `README.md:27-37`; `docs/reference/capabilities.md:1-17`; `AGENTS.md:292-309`; `docs/benchmarks/baseline-v1.md:80-93`; `docs/concepts/repository-identity.md:1-5`.

answers.q-canonical-knowledge: Canonical Repository Knowledge remains the source of truth. Search indexes, vector stores, and graph stores are rebuildable projections rather than canonical storage, and replacing a backend must not change FetchCore contract meaning. Canonical KnowledgeDocument and KnowledgeProvenance carry repository identity, revision, and source path.
answers.q-intent-scope: SearchIntent expresses what the caller means to retrieve; SearchScope defines where FetchCore may look. RetrievalConfig/policy separately controls how retrieval executes.
answers.q-required-semantics: The request is rejected when a channel cannot preserve required anchors or boolean/group structure. There is no configurable flattening fallback, and rejected structure is never concatenated into embedding text. Current hybrid retrieval likewise rejects hard anchors/groups because its dense-plus-fusion pipeline has no post-fusion constraint engine.
answers.q-backends: The named built-in retrieval adapters are local-semantic, solr, opensearch, and qdrant-vector. Ollama is also named, but as an embedding provider separate from the retrieval adapters.
answers.q-serving: Serving is backend-neutral and flows through the application service to CLI, MCP, and SDK/API consumers. MCP binds exactly one authorized repository per serving instance/request context, and the serving application resolves a RepositoryBinding and restricts source access to it. The recalled memory does not specify where backend-specific protocol details are allowed.
